sources.title: HarnessWAM: Bridging Prediction and Deliberation in World Action Models

omissions: Identity: the inspected title page identifies arXiv:2608.09516v1 [cs.RO], 10 August 2026. Its title and all eleven authors match the catalog; no revision or edition substitution is involved.
Text extraction does not reconstruct figure images; inspect the retained PDF for figures and equation/table layout.
The extraction limitation was addressed by visual inspection of Figures 1–3, Tables 1–4, and all pages supporting retained technical claims.
Separate supplemental material availability has not been fully verified.
No appendix is present in the supplied 15-page PDF. All five text chunks were read; references were read as supplied, without opening the cited works.
Code and external resources were not inspected; no training, inference, or reproduction experiment was run.

synopsis: HarnessWAM adds persistent scene evidence, constrained skill planning, event-triggered verification, and local recovery around LingBot-VA. Its matched-checkpoint comparisons support improved composition of manipulation skills; the strongest measured ablation concerns the interface that compiles semantic plans into executable operations.

problem.text: A finite-horizon controller can execute a local instruction yet lack the cross-stage knowledge needed to finish a partially observed task. In the drawer example, exploration must reveal the target before placement can be planned. The authors call this mismatch the prediction–deliberation gap.

contributions.text: An external runtime combines a VLM Task Manager, evidence-linked scene belief, task graph, deterministic executable-space projection, progress monitoring, and recovery without changing the WAM architecture.

The authors attribute improved task reliability to persistent orchestration beyond initial decomposition. Same-WAM comparisons and component removals support this system-level claim within the evaluated benchmarks.

inputs: Global natural-language instruction; agent-view and wrist-view RGB; robot proprioceptive state
Local skill instruction, finite observation history, and persistent task state
outputs: Continuous action chunks executed in the environment
Updated belief, memory, task graph, and event-level decisions; verified task outcome

steps.name: Maintain evidence and delayed bindings
steps.detail: Scene facts store subject, predicate, object, value, epistemic status, confidence, and supporting RGB evidence. Observed, inferred, and unknown facts remain distinct. Memory retains attempts, variable bindings, and revisions. A directed graph combines motor nodes with cognitive operations such as observing and verifying; unresolved targets remain symbolic until evidence supports binding.

steps.name: Compile within the executor’s capabilities
steps.detail: The deterministic compiler checks types, dependencies, preconditions and effects, single-arm holding state, and acyclicity. It expands supported compositions and canonicalizes nodes into local WAM instructions. PLACE requires prior acquisition of the same object. Infeasible plans return a failure symbol and violated constraints for replanning. Only the unexecuted graph suffix may change.

steps.name: Execute and detect candidate events
steps.detail: LingBot-VA generates action chunks from observations, robot state, and the active skill prompt. A separate estimator predicts continuous progress, completion likelihood, and progress-bin probabilities. Milestones, exhausted skill budgets, or changed conditions trigger deliberation; estimator output alone cannot complete a motor node.

steps.name: Verify, adapt, and recover
steps.detail: The Task Manager combines RGB, progress history, belief, graph, evidence, and execution state to continue, advance, observe, replan, recover, or terminate. Recovery drives joints and gripper toward their saved subtask-initial state, clears local WAM state, retains scene knowledge, and reprojects the remaining plan. It does not restore the environment.

training.text: LingBot-VA is fine-tuned separately on each benchmark’s training data with its architecture unchanged; controlled variants share that checkpoint. Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct serves as Task Manager without task-specific fine-tuning. RoboMemArena WAM RGB inputs are 256×256. Task Manager visual inputs exclude depth, segmentation, and privileged simulator state.

The progress model uses five timesteps of dual-view RGB and skill text. Frozen SigLIP2-base-patch16-256 features feed a four-layer causal Transformer. Supervision combines regression, interval classification, ranking, endpoint anchoring, completion prediction, and local monotonicity. Episodes separate training/validation; checkpoint selection minimizes validation progress error.

inference.text: Algorithm 1 initializes belief and memory, plans and projects a graph, then selects ready nodes. Cognitive nodes acquire evidence and reproject future work. Motor nodes execute chunks until an event decision changes execution. Success requires all required nodes plus final visual goal verification; infeasibility, termination, or budget exhaustion can yield failure.

equations.explanation: Equation (1): the WAM maps observation history, robot state, and the local skill instruction to an H-action chunk. These inputs are denoted by \(o_{\le t}\), \(q_t\), and \(g_k\); the output is \(A_t\). Figure 2 labels its last action \(a_{t+H}\); the equation supplies the explicit horizon definition.

Equation (12): the compiler projects the proposed graph into the intersection of the plan language generated by validated WAM primitives \(\mathcal{P}_W\) and the feasible set \(\mathcal{F}(z_k)\). Runtime state \(z_k\) contains belief, graph, memory, and active-skill execution state; feasibility depends on scene, bindings, dependencies, and embodiment. This specifies deterministic compilation.

results.setting: 26 tasks; HarnessWAM and same-WAM diagnostics use 20 rollouts per task with matched initial states, seeds, interfaces, and task budgets; macro-averaged across tasks and rollouts.
results.comparison: Whole Task: 44.4 / 52.3; Static Plan: 47.9 / 62.0; published PrediMem: 38.5 / 55.2.
results.interpretation: The gain over Static Plan is 11.7 / 7.9 percentage points. Full-task success requires all stage predicates; subtask success averages the completed fraction. Published baselines provide context with weaker experimental control.

results.setting: Table 1 task-family breakdown under the same-WAM protocol.
results.comparison: Static Plan: occlusion 38.2 / 49.8 and counting 67.2 / 90.1; published PrediMem transfer 22.5 / 45.2.
results.interpretation: Improvement is uneven: counting subtask success falls 1.9 points versus Static Plan, and transfer remains weak.

results.setting: Static, fully observable Ideal subset; official key object-state transition metric; published comparator scores.
results.interpretation: The 1.78-point lead over the strongest listed comparator concerns mean transition completion. It is not an all-stages full-task success rate and cannot be directly equated with RoboMemArena’s 59.6%.

results.setting: Matched LingBot-VA weights, initial states, and evaluation seeds; Table 3.
results.value: Full system 59.6 / 69.9; without projection 18.5 / 38.3; without progress events 38.3 / 50.7; without task state 47.7 / 61.1; progress-only switching 55.4 / 68.4; without recovery 54.2 / 67.7.
results.comparison: Projection removal costs 41.1 / 31.6 percentage points, the largest component-removal loss.
results.interpretation: This intervention jointly removes multiple checks. Fixed-interval deliberation changes event selection; equal VLM-call cost is not established.

results.setting: Raw, lexically normalized, and fully projected graphs; reference decompositions used only in offline analysis.
results.interpretation: Projection adds 30.6 executability points beyond normalization. These are intermediate plan diagnostics; sample size and uncertainty are unspecified.

limitations.text: The conclusion leaves real-world manipulation, broader validated skill repertoires, and calibrated uncertainty-aware deliberation to future work. Benchmark evidence does not establish physical deployment.

Tables 1–4 give no confidence intervals or dispersion. Hardware, latency, and VLM-call counts are unreported, limiting significance and efficiency conclusions. Recovery restores the robot toward a saved configuration but cannot undo environmental changes.

reproduction.text: Reproduction requires benchmark-specific LingBot-VA checkpoints, the named VLM and progress encoder, episode-separated progress training, a validated primitive inventory, graph compiler, event logic, and joint/gripper recovery control. Preserve matched initial states and budgets.

Optimizer schedules, dataset sizes/split ratios, loss weights, exact prompts, complete validated skill inventory, numerical event thresholds, budget settings, hardware, and software versions are unspecified. These remain implementation requirements; the illustrated checks are proposed experiments.

reasoning.text: The separate Qwen Task Manager and LingBot-VA executor support Dual-system; persistent state supports Memory & long-horizon modeling. Other mechanisms and Outside quadrants fit the contribution’s external compilation and verification loop: no new joint future/action predictor or inverse-dynamics decoder is introduced. Policy post-training is supported only by benchmark-specific fine-tuning; no WM-RL objective or reinforcement-learning procedure is established.

discussionQuestions: Does executable projection retain its advantage when prompt vocabulary, VLM calls, and execution budgets are matched?
Can event-triggered verification improve full-task success at the same deliberation cost, and how often does recovery encounter irreversible scene changes?

evidence.location: PDF p. 1, title, author/affiliation block, and arXiv margin identifier
evidence.detail: HarnessWAM: Bridging Prediction and Deliberation in World Action Models; eleven listed authors; arXiv:2608.09516v1 [cs.RO], 10 August 2026.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 1–2, Abstract, Section 1, and Figure 1/caption
evidence.detail: The prediction–deliberation gap concerns local WAM control versus persistent planning, evidence retention, verification, and recovery; Figure 1 illustrates sequential drawer exploration.

evidence.location: PDF p. 4, Figure 2/caption and Section 3.1, Equations (1)–(3)
evidence.detail: The architecture connects an external Task Manager, task state, deterministic compiler, WAM, runtime, and environment. Equation (1) ends an H-action chunk at a(t+H−1); Figure 2 labels its endpoint a(t+H). Runtime state contains belief, graph, memory, and active-skill execution state.

Evidence-linked facts distinguish observed, inferred, and unknown state; memory stores attempts and revisions; motor/cognitive graph nodes carry preconditions, effects, termination, recovery, and delayed entity bindings.

The extensible ontology is restricted to empirically validated WAM primitives. Deterministic compilation enforces types, dependencies, holding-state and precondition/effect consistency, and acyclicity; infeasible graphs return a failure symbol; executed history remains invariant.

Progress, completion probability, and progress intervals are estimated from recent dual-view RGB and skill text. Six supervision terms train the estimator; milestones, budgets, and changed conditions trigger deliberation without directly advancing nodes.

evidence.location: PDF p. 7, Algorithm 1, lines 1–38, and Equation (16)
evidence.detail: Inference initializes and projects a graph; handles cognitive and motor nodes; executes environment actions; event decisions include continue, advance, observe, replan, recover, and terminate. Required nodes plus final goal verification govern success.

Recovery targets saved arm/gripper state with multi-step control, clears local WAM state, retains environment and memory, and reprojects subsequent plans. Task execution and recovery budgets bound termination.
RoboMemArena has 26 tasks across transfer, occlusion, counting, and sequence; RoboCerebra Ideal evaluates long-horizon compositional manipulation.
RoboMemArena full-task success requires all stage predicates; subtask success averages the within-task completed fraction. RoboCerebra SR averages key object-state transition completion.

evidence.location: PDF p. 9, Section 4.1, Evaluation protocol and Baselines
evidence.detail: HarnessWAM and same-WAM diagnostics use 20 rollouts per task with matched initial states, seeds, observation interfaces, and budgets. Published scores come from benchmark evaluations. Whole Task lacks decomposition; Static Plan fixes its initial linear sequence.

evidence.location: PDF p. 9, Section 4.1, Models and implementation details
evidence.detail: Benchmark-specific LingBot-VA fine-tuning preserves architecture. Qwen3-VL-32B-Instruct is not task-fine-tuned. The progress estimator uses five timesteps, frozen SigLIP2-base-patch16-256, and a four-layer causal Transformer; episodes separate training and validation.

evidence.location: PDF p. 10, Table 1, all rows and task-family/average SR columns; Section 4.2
evidence.detail: HarnessWAM average task/subtask scores are 59.6/69.9, versus Static Plan 47.9/62.0 and Whole Task 44.4/52.3. PrediMem averages 38.5/55.2 and leads transfer at 22.5/45.2. HarnessWAM counting subtask score 88.2 trails Static Plan 90.1.

evidence.location: PDF p. 10, Table 2, Ideal SR column, and Section 4.2, RoboCerebra paragraph
evidence.detail: Ideal SR is 23.70 for HarnessWAM, 21.92 for GPT-4o Planner + OpenVLA, 21.10 for HPE, 7.84 for OpenVLA, and 1.88 for π0.5. Ideal is described as static and fully observable.

evidence.location: PDF pp. 10–11, Section 4.3 intervention definitions; p. 11, Table 3, all rows and columns
evidence.detail: Average task/subtask scores: full 59.6/69.9; no task state 47.7/61.1; no projection 18.5/38.3; no progress events 38.3/50.7; progress-only 55.4/68.4; no recovery 54.2/67.7. Sequential progress-only switching yields 72.5/97.9 versus full 86.3/93.0. Fixed-interval invocation replaces progress events; no recovery terminates on failure or budget exhaustion.

evidence.location: PDF p. 11, Table 4, all rows/columns, and Section 4.3, Plan-level diagnosis
evidence.detail: Raw/normalized/projected syntax: 60.8/84.6/95.2; dependencies: 58.1/67.5/92.9; binding: 21.3/63.8/88.3; executability: 13.8/42.3/72.9. Reference decompositions support offline analysis only, never inference. Sample counts and uncertainty are not reported here.

Ten selected Task 4 keyframes show exploration of top, middle, and bottom drawers, followed by reopening the non-empty top drawer and picking/placing the cookie. The caption attributes target retention to stored evidence.
Real-world manipulation, broader WAM skill repertoires, and calibrated uncertainty-aware deliberation are identified as future directions.
